scope: Bounded 11-destination common-definition review; no contacts or main-array writes. Product: purchased personal postal 100g Japan-made sealed plain industrially steamed/rolled/dried Camellia tea. No permits, certificates, special registration or advance agency notice; ordinary customs and arrival inspection accepted.

standardEvidence.provision: ISPM 32 normative Category 1 rules, read with Appendix 2 Category 1 tea illustration (Чай), printed page 32-18.
standardEvidence.qualification: Appendix 2 is explicitly reference-only and non-prescriptive. This is commodity evidence interpreted through operative national law, not a directly binding international country exemption. The page dated 28 July 2025 links an older standard version; do not call this a new 2025 enactment.

results.finding: Recovered full Proclamation 156/2006. Article 3(22) risk-qualifies manufactured plant products. Article 4(2)(g–h) requires prohibited/restricted lists and the justification of phytosanitary measures to be based on PRA or applicable international standards; Article 17 repeats that standard for new restrictions. This is an operative standards reference, not merely IPPC membership. It supports the manufactured-tea exclusion interpretation, but its immediate subject is list-making/justification rather than a general interpretation rule or an all-inspection compliance command. No contrary tea measure was recovered. The pass does not demand a bespoke ruling and submits this distinction for peer review.
results.remainingEvidence: Determine whether the operative list-making/measure-justification standard, together with Article 3(22) and ISPM 32 tea Category 1, adequately determines nonregulated manufacturing scope under the general import clauses; the current public material does not expose the applicable list. Existing general trade-notice applicability to a paid own-consumption postal purchase also remains recorded.
results.classificationNote: A positive combined-source inference remains a peer-review question, not ruled out simply for lack of tea naming.

results.finding: The official current index confirms Proclamation 1400/2026, in force from 7 May 2026. Full operative plant-law text is not available in the reviewed local corpus; the known Ministry PDF previously returned access failure. This pass checked the current official index and precise indexed provision searches without repeating the same failed full-text fetch. It cannot establish or disprove an operative international-definition clause. The old 1992 law must not be substituted.
results.remainingEvidence: The complete enacted current Proclamation 1400/2026, particularly definitions, import scope, standards-incorporation and processing provisions. Separately, current private-food scope under Proclamation 1112/2019 and implementing EFDA rules remains as in the existing row.

results.finding: Recovered the complete four-page Law L/92/027/CTRN from the official IPPC reporting file, visually read all pages and OCRed them. Article 2 risk-qualifies manufactured plant products; no default ISPM interpretation provision appears in the full law. Published NPPO procedure PR01-23 section 4 expressly cites NIMP 5 and 32, and section 5 directs officers to apply the procedure: an actual operational standards reference, stronger than membership. This materially supports a Category 1 processing interpretation; it still does not remove the independently unresolved 2024 BNIQ transport/private-use scope.
results.remainingEvidence: The signed BNIQ Order A/2024/920 Articles 3–4 leave actual air-post transport coverage and automatic versus discretionary non-sale/noncommercial exemption unsettled. Article 6 origin documents apply if that route covers the parcel. The common plant standard alone cannot answer this independent duty.
results.accessNote: The NPPO procedure was read in the web indexed full-text reader (66 lines, reference turn2061view0); direct downloads from the two Ministry hosts returned 503 and 429 error bodies and are not source PDFs.

results.finding: Existing official material concerns regional land-border trade and automated customs, not a plant-product definition or standards-incorporation provision. No full current plant law was available to test a definition bridge. No generic repeat search or membership-based conclusion was made.
results.remainingEvidence: An operative national plant law/commodity rule defining manufactured plant products and the applicable private postal route; neither regional border measures nor a postal prohibited-items list supplies that missing scope.

results.finding: Read Decree-Law 4/99 Article 2(b), Articles 7–8 and Article 16. The plant-product definition is unprocessed goods or simple preparation, without an operative ISPM definition adoption or examples determining steam-manufactured tea. IPPC reference is preambular. Article 16 leaves interpretation disputes to ministerial order; that is not a processing exemption. The food law delegates documentary methods rather than itself establishing a private certificate.
results.remainingEvidence: A general binding processing interpretation or applicable implementing rule defining simple preparation for industrially steamed/rolled/dried tea. A personal ruling is not intrinsically required; any operative general rule would suffice.

results.finding: Operative Plant Law Articles 3–4, 39 and 46 create a domestic route for the ISPM 32 tea Category 1 classification; full private food-law review does not establish a separate special-document duty for plain tea. Proposed conditional support retains exact label and ordinary customs/arrival conditions.

Article 9(c) requires international phytosanitary standards compliance; Articles 1(29/30/38) risk-qualify scope. This bridges actual ISPM 32 tea Category 1 and industrial processing to nonregulated goods. Article 12(2) does not create control merely because a good is unlisted; it covers unlisted controlled goods. The Portuguese original Article 17 does not impose advance inspection on all nonregulated imports. PAC 98/2023 Article 4 expressly exempts postal parcels.

The 1976 Notice has a real cooked-food exception, and a reading cooked OR (pickled and bottled/canned) is linguistically possible. The exception is expressly for purposes of this Notice issued under Rule 9 of the parent 1974 Rules. The full parent Rules were not recovered in this bounded exact search; the Notice alone cannot establish absence of an independent parent-rule permit duty. A secondary review quotes a broad parent Rule 2, but was used only as a retrieval lead, not as the legal conclusion. No operative ISPM definition bridge was recovered.
results.remainingEvidence: The complete parent Plant Phytosanitary (Import) Rules, P.N.66/1974, including definitions, Rule 2 and interaction with Rule 9/1976 Notice, plus a defensible application of the cooked-food clause to steam-manufactured tea in pouches. This is a legal-text/scope gap, not a demand for a bespoke tea ruling.

results.finding: Law 96-007 expressly includes dried material; Decree 98-099 Articles 27–28 leave documentary prescriptions to ministerial measures. The 2011 fee order actually names imported tea for inspection, so ISPM 32 cannot be treated as displacing a contrary domestic processing scope. Examined international references do not establish general ISPM definition priority. The inspection fee itself is not a certificate requirement.
results.remainingEvidence: The operative documentary prescription applicable to a one-off private postal tea parcel, and whether the prior-declaration/annual economic-operator procedure has a personal scope or exception.

results.finding: Recovered and read the complete Plant Protection and Health Act 2015. The risk-qualified manufactured-product definition is present, but the identified international guideline provision, section 5(2)(g), is specifically about new germplasm screening at post-entry quarantine stations. It is not an operative general definition adoption for food. SI4/2020 supplies covered-goods permit procedures without a manufacturing exemption. The independent UNBS alternative destination-inspection route remains separately unresolved.
results.remainingEvidence: A general applicable processing/classification rule or broader operative standards bridge for manufactured tea; separately, the private postal availability of UNBS regulation 7 destination inspection using ordinary customs only.

results.finding: St Helena and Ascension positive routes do not determine Tristan da Cunha rules. The 2021 Tristan Biosecurity Ordinance is marked not yet in force in the government consolidation, and no commencement evidence is available. Island Council section 15/Schedule 3(f) authorizes live/dead-plant by-laws but does not itself classify this food. An uncommenced modern definition cannot supply the missing operative bridge.
results.remainingEvidence: Operative Tristan by-laws/commencement and general scope of the live/dead-plants import warning for factory-manufactured tea; the whole SH destination code cannot be cleared from two islands alone.

limitations: Current international tea illustration is reference-only; each proposal supplies the operative domestic bridge and actual product-processing inference.
No proof of nonexistence of hypothetical delegated measures was required.
No business-only duties were transferred to private consumers.
Failures and missing full laws remain explicit rather than being treated as negative substantive rules.
